precise_scope: For every actual reference in a pseudoeffective zero-volume class on connected smooth compact Kähler X, the degree-d full-mass and joint linear finite-energy domains are common to all auxiliary Kähler classes/forms. On this genuine F1 domain, finite truncation/cocycle energies extend coefficientwise to homogeneous degree-(n-d) class polynomials. Their functional span equals the bounded-type span, giving the exact necessary/sufficient minimum energy-family reference q(lambda^(n-d)) in Sym^(n-d)H^(1,1)/Ann(S), retaining raw mass and compatible with same-type anchors, theta gauge and decreasing coefficient continuity. The uncontrolled unbounded moving-form perturbation assertion remains false; original closure is not claimed.
limitations: Original P15.1 remains open: the proved minimum is relative to a prescribed actual bounded type and this particular common F1 energy family, not an independently geometric universal minimum reference for every zero-volume theory.

The unrestricted unbounded class-convergent moving-representative leading perturbation assertion is false by the reconstructed analytic concentration example; general moving unbounded-potential or joint limits require a separate valid prescription and proof.

Degree-d finite joint energy has not here been proved to control all lower-degree weighted perturbation coefficients, even for arbitrary fixed forms and reference types; no unrestricted unbounded path/differential calculus or increasing continuity is claimed.
The leading scale uses actual-current mass coefficients, not a general leading class-volume coefficient theorem or an identification of actual degree with class numerical dimension.

The carrier is explicitly X of dimension n with product bidegree (d,d); no geometric d-dimensional carrier or general geometric/factorwise kernel classification is constructed. P15.2/P15.3 and optional d=0 rigidity are not investigated.

result.report:
The supplied argument establishes the exact scoped continuation. This verdict does not assert original catalogue closure or the excluded unrestricted unbounded moving-form perturbation limit. Prior reviews, status labels, hashes, compilations and finite diagnostics supply no mathematical assumptions.

The actual degree is established correctly. Pointwise comparison of Kähler forms makes positivity of each trace mass independent of the auxiliary form. The current P+εω represents a big class, so mixed mass monotonicity bounds its top mass by the minimal-singularity volume. Its nonnegative binomial expansion and the boundary volume limit force M_n=0; M_0>0 gives 0≤d<n. Every mixed mass comparison uses exactly n slots, filling complementary slots with smooth Kähler forms and zero potentials. Consequently higher-degree products of more-singular currents vanish by zero positive trace mass. Closedness and smooth Stokes give the stated mass polynomials. This uses actual-current multilinearity, never class positive-product multilinearity. The relevant scopes are confirmed in [BEGZ](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2) and [DDNL](https://msp.org/apde/2018/11-8/apde-v11-n8-p06-s.pdf).

The normalization and bounded integration-by-parts reconstruction check. DDNL potentials must be divided by 2π; Vu potentials must be divided by 2. Vu's source gradient is then half the argument's gradient, so multiplying source IBP by two gives exactly (I). The intrinsic square identity has coefficient 1/2, and the local square coefficients are 1,1,−1/2. The printed omissions cannot be used literally. With the correct identity, the supplied cutoff satisfies ∫dζ_k∧d^cζ_k R≤(4/k)∫ΩR, while the truncated difference gradients have uniformly bounded mass. Cauchy–Schwarz therefore removes the cutoff derivative terms. Admissibility, finite-locus locality and dominated convergence justify the remaining limits. The bounded starting calculus is also justified by BEGZ Theorem 1.14 with empty exceptional set. Thus this reconstruction does not depend on the defective repeated formulas in [Vu v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.13241v3).

For bounded type, multilinearity makes the finite-dimensional one-form polynomial. IBP makes its cross derivatives equal; Stokes on triangles gives the cocycle. The beta integral supplies precisely 1/(q+1), and the diagonal Dirichlet product gives the claimed concavity sign. Constants and monotonicity give the raw-mass translation and Lipschitz laws. Changing a complementary representative transfers dd^c to the bounded potential difference; both resulting (d+1)-fold products vanish. The smooth real primitive needed here has exactly the hypotheses of the [DGMS dd^c lemma](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~dennis/publications/PDF/DS-pub-0024.pdf). Expansion into differences of Kähler forms then gives a well-defined symmetric class functional. The perturbation expansion and subset-counting coefficient identity are correct, including the lower-degree bounds and the bounded moving-potential error estimate.

The common full-mass proof is valid without positivity of a current difference. Choosing D_0=Aω_0−ω_1 Kähler makes every scalar mixed deficit Δ_j nonnegative by the slotwise DDNL theorem. Their positively weighted sum is zero, so each deficit vanishes. Polynomial extraction subsequently gives equality for arbitrary mixed complementary Kähler factors. Pointwise comparison of those factors compares the positive weighted measures and proves auxiliary independence of finite joint linear energy.

The relative-energy identification has the correct scope. For d≥1, Vu's common reference may be an arbitrary actual positive current; minimal or model singularities are not required. Here R=ω^(n−d) is smooth positive and the relative product is top degree. Connectedness makes cohomology equality equivalent to scalar mass equality. With χ(t)=t, the source joint energy is exactly (d/2) times the binomial-weighted sum in (6). Its finiteness is therefore precisely the proposed F¹ condition. Vu's diagonal full-mass and weighted convexity theorems apply. Averaging a finite family, expanding its positive product and comparing each mixed mass with M_d proves all mixed full-mass equalities. The weighted average similarly proves integrability of every family difference against every required mixed measure.

The truncation identity (7) is exact. Original and truncated measures agree on the strict comparison set and have equal total mass; their complementary masses therefore agree. On the complement, the truncated weight is exactly L, including the equality boundary. Monotone convergence proves both the finite truncation limit and its equivalence with (6). Constants correctly handle potentials initially bounded above by ψ+C.

The continuity proof respects both published boundedness restrictions. General decreasing capacity convergence is reconstructed from bounded truncations and the GZ sublevel estimate; it is not attributed directly to bounded Proposition 3.7. In each local weighted convergence application, every product factor is first bounded, all n slots are present, and the cutoff weights are bounded, quasicontinuous and capacity convergent. Equal total masses control the omitted tail. Likewise, Vu Theorem 3.3 is used only after bounding all product factors and then exhausting simultaneous finite loci. These applications match [GZ](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~guedj/fichierspdf/JGA05.pdf), DDNL Proposition 2.2 and Vu's bounded comparison theorem.

Decreasing continuity on F¹ follows from the stated truncation sandwich. Concavity then follows from bounded concavity and decreasing approximations. For the unbounded cocycle, equality of mixed tail masses and the bound Lν_{a,L}(B_L)≤∫_{B_L}(z_u+z_v)dν_a make the truncated tail vanish; mixed weighted integrability also removes the original tail. Passing the bounded cocycle to the limit gives (11). No unbounded IBP is invoked.

The coefficient extension and minimum quotient are established. Kähler powers span Sym^m V because a homogeneous polynomial vanishing on the open Kähler cone is zero. Selecting a basis of such powers gives finitely many unisolvent evaluations. Their finite truncation limits force coefficient convergence through a fixed inverse linear map. Mixed positive-factor truncation limits, followed by finite signed expansions, establish the explicit unbounded integral formula and polarization. Since the bounded span S is finite-dimensional and closed, every unbounded functional lies in S; bounded potentials already belong to F¹, so the two spans coincide. This proves both directions of (18), the linear universal factorization, and the corresponding minimum informational descriptor on the Kähler cone.

Raw mass survives through the constant potential ψ+1. Hence Ann(S) is contained in the mass kernel and Q is nonzero. Same-type anchors have identical domains and masses; the proved cocycle gives the functional anchor law and equality of their spans and annihilators. Smooth theta gauge changes preserve currents, differences and truncations. Finite bounded energy coordinates determine the quotient topology. Decreasing coefficient convergence gives uniform convergence on compact class sets and continuity of the stated simultaneous quotient pairing.

All degree-zero cases are covered independently: full mass is automatic, quasi-psh local integrability gives F¹=E, energies are affine smooth-volume integrals, and the truncation, cocycle, representative, constant, anchor and gauge laws remain valid. No k=0 application of Vu's weighted theorem and no rigidity assertion about C_ψ is needed.

The examples also check analytically. The logarithmic-power potential has vanishing pole flux and finite weighted singular-current integral exactly when the displayed integral ∫s^(2a−2)ds converges. The concentration construction has finite energy and full perturbed mass at every fixed ε, but its extra term ε∫vκ_ε tends to −∞. It therefore refutes precisely the excluded uncontrolled perturbation extension while leaving the degree-d polynomial theorem intact. The divisor example correctly distinguishes actual degree zero from nef numerical dimension one and from the leading class-volume exponent. The product-surface quotient computation gives S equal to the span of the B coordinate, with constants supplying that coordinate.

Harmless wording qualifications are explicit: cutoff locality concerns the nonzero locus, not necessarily closed support; GZ 3.7 has bounded hypotheses; Vu 3.3 has bounded product factors. The continuation already supplies the needed truncation deductions and the intrinsic half-factor correction. No substantial repair of its substantive argument is required.

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler n-fold, the nonpluripolar product of any k closed positive (1,1)-currents, 1≤k≤n, is finite, positive, closed, symmetric, multilinear under sums of positive currents and plurifinely local. Its coefficient measures do not charge pluripolar sets. Locally it is determined by the bounded Bedford–Taylor truncation products on simultaneous strict finite loci; smooth positive factors are ordinary wedge factors. BEGZ, Definition 1.1, Propositions 1.4 and 1.6, Theorem 1.8.

passages.statement: A big class on a compact Kähler manifold has positive currents with minimal singularities, less singular than every positive current in that class, and its volume is their top nonpluripolar mass. Positive products of pseudoeffective classes are defined by the limits obtained by adding ε times any Kähler class, independently of that Kähler class; in particular vol(α+ελ)→vol(α) as ε↓0. Positive products of nef classes equal ordinary cup products. BEGZ, Sections 1.3–1.4 and Definition 1.17.

premises: On a compact Kähler n-fold, the nonpluripolar product of any k closed positive (1,1)-currents, 1≤k≤n, is finite, positive, closed, symmetric, multilinear under sums of positive currents and plurifinely local. Its coefficient measures do not charge pluripolar sets. Locally it is determined by the bounded Bedford–Taylor truncation products on simultaneous strict finite loci; smooth positive factors are ordinary wedge factors. BEGZ, Definition 1.1, Propositions 1.4 and 1.6, Theorem 1.8.

On a compact Kähler n-fold, let θ_j be smooth closed real (1,1)-forms with pseudoeffective classes and u_j,v_j∈PSH(X,θ_j), 1≤j≤n. Their top mixed nonpluripolar integrals are equal when corresponding potentials have the same singularity type in every slot. The u-integral is at least the v-integral when u_j is less singular than v_j in every slot. DDNL, Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 2.4; their convention is θ_u=θ+i∂bar∂u.

A big class on a compact Kähler manifold has positive currents with minimal singularities, less singular than every positive current in that class, and its volume is their top nonpluripolar mass. Positive products of pseudoeffective classes are defined by the limits obtained by adding ε times any Kähler class, independently of that Kähler class; in particular vol(α+ελ)→vol(α) as ε↓0. Positive products of nef classes equal ordinary cup products. BEGZ, Sections 1.3–1.4 and Definition 1.17.

On a compact Kähler n-fold, for a closed positive current R of bidegree (n−1,n−1), bounded R-admissible dsh functions a,b have finite, representation-independent intrinsic Dirichlet products, positive on the diagonal, and satisfy ∫b〈dd^ca dot R〉=∫a〈dd^cb dot R〉=−∫〈db∧d^ca dot R〉. Admissibility means that the poles of representing quasi-psh functions have zero R trace mass. Relative nonpluripolar products are associative in admissible bidegrees and preserve absence of mass on locally complete pluripolar sets uncharged by their base current. Vu v3, Proposition 2.1, Lemmas 2.5–2.6 and Theorem 2.7. Vu's convention is d^c=i(bar∂−∂)/(2π), dd^c=i∂bar∂/π.

On a compact Kähler manifold, a smooth differential form that is d-closed, d^c-closed and d-exact is dd^c-exact. This statement holds for real as well as complex forms. DGMS, Lemma 5.11 and Remark 5.14.

On a compact Kähler manifold, let P be an actual closed positive (1,1)-current in a pseudoeffective class and R a closed positive current, with k≥1 and k+deg(R)≤n. Relative full mass for k-tuples of more-singular currents in the reference class means equality of relative-product cohomology classes. For convex increasing χ with χ(−∞)=−∞, normalized negative potentials u_j≤φ define joint χ-energy as Σ_J∫−χ(Σ_j(u_j−φ))〈Π_{j∈J}S_j Π_{j∉J}P dot R〉. Its finiteness is independent of finite potential constants. The diagonal full-mass and weighted classes are convex, and the weighted class is unchanged by a cohomologous same-singularity-type common reference. Vu v3, Section 3, Corollary 3.2 and Theorem 3.4.

For a Kähler background Ω on a compact Kähler n-fold, global Monge–Ampère capacity satisfies a negative Ω-psh sublevel bound of order (∫|f|Ω^n+n∫Ω^n)/A for {f<−A}. Decreasing bounded Ω-psh functions with bounded limit converge in this capacity. Ω-psh functions are quasicontinuous, and global capacity is comparable to local Bedford–Taylor capacities on a finite relatively compact chart cover. Guedj–Zeriahi, Propositions 3.6, 3.7 and 3.10 and Corollary 3.8.

On an open subset of C^n, uniformly bounded psh factors in all n slots converging in capacity, together with uniformly bounded quasicontinuous weights converging in capacity to a quasicontinuous weight, have weakly convergent weighted Bedford–Taylor top products. DDNL, Proposition 2.2.

Let R be a closed positive current on an open subset U⊂C^n. If bounded psh product factors u_j,u'_j agree on W=∩_i{v_i>v'_i}, where the finitely many comparison potentials v_i,v'_i are psh and may be unbounded, then their Bedford–Taylor products relative to R agree after restriction to W. Vu v3, Theorem 3.3.

For bounded Ω-psh φ_1,φ_2 and a=φ_1−φ_2, ∫da∧d^ca∧R≤2‖a‖∞∫Ω∧R. Locally, bounded psh v and smooth f satisfy d(f(v)R)=f'(v)dv∧R. BEGZ, Lemma 1.9 and Theorem 1.14 with empty exceptional set; Vu v3, Equation (2.3) and Lemma 2.4.
